title: Ian Lind: Don't Be Steered Astray — You Do Need A Driver's License - Honolulu Civil Beat
summary: Hawaii columnist debunks a 'Freedom Ride' right-to-travel protest by checking the court cases its promoters cite.

assertions.quote: The U.S. Supreme Court has long held that states have the power to regulate the use of motor vehicles on their roadways.
does not provide a fundamental right to operate a motor vehicle
they actually offer no support for the idea that driver’s licenses are somehow unconstitutional
Then they simply, and falsely, say that since these specific laws don’t apply to personal vehicles, there are no licensing, insurance or other requirements
Two men were cited and arrested, and their vehicles towed by police.
an industry that intends to deceive in order to cynically sell an ideology as well as a wide range of how-to manuals, workshops and seminars
selectively quoting court decisions wildly out of context, turning their meanings inside out

verdicts.note: The stock citations (Thompson v. Smith, Chicago Motor Coach) concern other issues and themselves allow road regulation.
